title: Hydrothermally synthesised Nd 2 Te 4 O 11  nanosheets for broadband visible light photodetection and optical switching application
content: Wide-bandgap semiconducting materials are essential for improving electronic devices and energy storage applications. As rare-earth tellurium oxides belong to the wide-bandgap group, they will be impactful for optoelectronic applications. Neodymium oxotellurate (IV) (NTO) samples were synthesized via the hydrothermal method, with varying concentrations of Nd and Te. We varied the concentration ratios of Nd and Te in 1 : 1, 1 : 2, and 1 : 3 proportions, and the corresponding samples were NTO-1, NTO-2, and NTO-3, respectively. The Nd2Te4O11 structure in the monoclinic system was obtained from XRD analysis for all samples. Morphological analysis revealed nanorod and nanosheet structures, and the presence of the constituent elements was confirmed by EDX. Raman peaks were obtained for all samples in the low-frequency region. The XPS study was performed to determine the oxidation states. Optical studies of materials showed a narrowing of the band gap from 4.16 eV to 3.64 eV. The photosensitivity, responsivity, and detectivity of samples increased with an increase in Te concentration, exhibiting good photoresponse behaviour. The nonlinear optical (NLO) study indicated that the nonlinear refractive response was dominant over nonlinear absorption for all samples. This makes Nd2Te4O11 a multifunctional material suitable for broadband photodetectors, all nonlinear optical devices, and optical switching applications.
